[Needle Inspector — DevTools and MCP for three.js](#needle-inspector-devtools-and-mcp-for-three.js)
===================================================================================================

The **Needle Inspector** brings Chrome DevTools for three.js to your browser. Use this free Chrome extension to inspect and debug three.js, React Three Fiber (react-three-fiber), and Needle Engine scenes with WebGL and WebGPU renderers. Think of it as the browser's built-in inspector for 3D scenes: explore the scene hierarchy, inspect properties, and track performance. Needle Inspector Pro adds live property editing on development servers, memory and leak tools, AI editing via MCP, and export.

This extension in 5 minutes helped me solving a visual issue I was struggling to fix for two weeks. A must have for all ThreeJS devs

![Testimonial](/docs/inspector/testimonial-FrancescoMichelini.jpg)

Francesco MicheliniChrome Web Store Review, Dec 2025

### [Quick Start](#quick-start)

1.  Install the extension from the [Chrome Web Store](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/needle-inspector-%E2%80%94-devtoo/jonplpbnhmanoekkgcepnedhghflblmo)
2.  Open a webpage with a three.js scene.
3.  Click the Needle icon in the browser toolbar to enable the Inspector for that site. The page reloads.
4.  When the Inspector detects a scene, browse the hierarchy and select an object to inspect its properties.

Click the toolbar icon again to disable the Inspector for that site. This also reloads the page.

Inspect three.js websites

You can inspect three.js, React Three Fiber, and Needle Engine scenes on public websites as well as your own projects. Use it to understand how a scene is built or investigate a production issue.

A must have tool for pros, beginners, and everything in between!

![Testimonial](/docs/testimonial/placeholder.svg)

KidsFab productionChrome Web Store Review, Jan 2026

![Needle Inspector on the three.js examples page — scene hierarchy, AI chat, node graph, resources and code panel around a running scene](/docs/inspector/overview-needle-inspector.webp)

[Features](#features)
---------------------

### [Real-time Scene Inspection](#real-time-scene-inspection)

Browse your 3D scene hierarchy, similar to how the browser's Elements panel shows your HTML structure. Scene hierarchy inspection is free.

![Scene hierarchy in the Needle Inspector — browsing objects, meshes, lights and cameras of a live three.js scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/7dkT_1C-SETizR1mieW05A.gif)

*   **Scene Hierarchy**: Browse all objects, meshes, lights and cameras in an expandable tree view
*   **Search & Filter**: Quickly find objects by name or type
*   **Live Updates**: The tree follows your scene in real time as objects spawn, move and unload
*   **Isolated Inspect View**: Right-click any object to view it alone in a dedicated 3D view

### [Live Property Editing](#live-property-editing)

Tweak transforms, materials, lights and textures on the running scene and watch it react — every change goes through a real command system, so **Ctrl+Z / Cmd+Z undo works** like in a desktop editor.

![Live property editing in the Needle Inspector — tweaking materials on a running three.js scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/_qT6InzdSGJJWnDR4OZgZg.gif)

*   **Transforms**: Position, rotation and scale with draggable number inputs
*   **Materials**: Colors, maps, opacity, emission, roughness/metalness and rendering flags — including values baked into your GLBs that no code sets
*   **Textures**: Preview, inspect and swap texture slots
*   **Visibility & Flags**: Show/hide objects, toggle features live

Property editing is free on ordinary public websites. Editing on localhost, LAN development servers, and supported development, preview, and staging hosts requires [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Free-Fly Camera](#free-fly-camera)

Explore the scene from another angle. Click the camera icon in the top right to enable the fly camera, then use WASD to move through the scene. The camera remembers its last position and restores it when you return.

![Free-fly camera in the Needle Inspector — moving through a running three.js scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/BpvuEmacbFta1Bd5kiovuQ.gif)

#### [Inspect Above HTML and Change the Background](#inspect-above-html-and-change-the-background)

The fly camera can display the scene above the website's HTML, so page content no longer blocks your view. You can also temporarily expand the canvas to fill the browser viewport during inspection. Keep the website background or switch to a neutral light or dark checkerboard to inspect transparency, edges, and post-processing effects more clearly.

![Fly camera displaying a three.js scene above website content and switching between the website background and light and dark checkerboards](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/3dlbe4M7nU3ctMQJvvztIQ.gif)

### [Camera Animation Timeline](#camera-animation-timeline)

Open the **Animation** workspace to build a camera move while viewing the live scene. Use the free-fly camera to frame a view, add a camera clip, then capture more views as keyframes. Drag keys to change their timing, scrub or play the timeline to preview the move, and move or trim clips to arrange shots with hard cuts. Select a clip or keyframe to edit it in the Inspector.

Camera animations are saved locally for the inspected page. Camera animation is limited in the free version. [Pro](#free-vs-pro) supports longer sequences and lets you import or export the camera animation as JSON from the camera track menu. This JSON file is separate from the [scene GLB export](#save-and-export-changes). The timeline currently animates the Inspector camera, not arbitrary scene objects.

### [AI-Powered Assistance

![VS Code Logo](/docs/imgs/vscode-logo.webp "VS Code Logo") ![Claude Logo](/docs/imgs/claude-logo.webp "Claude Logo") ![Cursor Logo](/docs/imgs/cursor-logo.webp "Cursor Logo") ![Antigravity Logo](/docs/imgs/antigravity-logo.webp "Antigravity Logo")](#ai-powered-assistance)   

Let your AI assistant **inspect and edit the running three.js scene**. Use the built-in AI chat or connect an MCP client such as Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, or Antigravity.

![AI chat in the Needle Inspector — asking questions about the running three.js scene and editing it with AI](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/eycVjikaWUeHS86A3HfP4g.gif)

*   **MCP Integration**: Your agent reads the hierarchy, inspects objects, changes properties, and pulls your pending edits (`get_edits`) to apply them to your source code
*   **Built-in AI Chat**: Ask questions about the open scene without leaving the browser
*   **Available tools**: View the MCP tool list in the Inspector settings. Some tools are specific to the built-in chat or available only in certain contexts.

#### [Ask AI about anything](#ask-ai-about-anything)

Right-click any object in the **hierarchy** or the **3D scene** — or any **property in the inspector** — and _Ask AI about this_. The chat opens as a small bubble pinned to the thing you asked about, so the AI already has the context, and you can keep several conversations going at once while you work.

![Contextual AI chat bubbles in the Needle Inspector — asking about an object straight from the three.js scene, hierarchy or inspector](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/QH2pLpoBMHb9MxSs6VCX6Q.gif)

Setup is simple:

    npx needle-cloud start

Keep the terminal open, then connect your AI client to `http://localhost:8424/mcp`. **Learn how to connect your local AI tools**: [Needle MCP documentation](../ai/needle-mcp-server).

MCP & AI editing is part of [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Save and Export Changes](#save-and-export-changes)

Use these tools to save changes made to the running scene:

*   **Save and Load Edits**: Use **File → Save Edits** to export your edits as JSON, and **File → Load Edits** to load them back into the Inspector. Hand the JSON to an AI agent to apply the changes to your local project's source code, or share it with a team member. You can also save a readable text version.
*   **Edits via MCP**: A connected AI agent can read your edits directly with `get_edits` and apply them to your project's source code.
*   **GLB Export**: Export objects or whole scenes as glTF/GLB — **textures and animations included**
*   **Texture Export**: Right-click any texture slot to download that texture as a PNG
*   **Undo History**: Undo and redo edits made through the Inspector command system

![Exporting Inspector edits to JSON and loading edits from JSON to share changes with an AI agent or team member](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/csWFKkAIFwPggN1L2-v9sA.gif)![Right-clicking a texture slot to export the texture as a PNG in the Needle Inspector](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/7f7aI5PTXntuxFr107YJQA.gif)

Saving edits, GLB export, and texture export require [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Performance Panel](#performance-panel)

Track frame rate, memory use, and rendering work over time. Pause the graphs to investigate a spike.

![Performance panel in the Needle Inspector — live FPS, CPU and GPU memory, render passes, draw calls and triangles for a running three.js scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/Zl1RM8T4tCkgrLo-W2QZzA.gif)

*   **FPS, CPU memory and GPU memory (VRAM)** as running graphs, with the current value next to each
*   **Render passes, draw calls and triangles per frame** — the GPU's real work, counted across every pass (shadows, prepass, post-processing), not just the scene's raw triangle count
*   **Potential VRAM saving**: how much texture memory compression would reclaim
*   **In scene vs. loaded**: meshes, geometries, materials and textures that are actually in the current scene, next to everything the page has loaded
*   **Events**: jank and big loads marked on the timeline — a long frame names the function and file behind it, and in local development you can **jump straight to the line of code** that caused the stall
*   **Pause** at any moment to read the numbers behind a spike

### [Resources & Memory](#resources-memory)

Inspect loaded textures, geometries, and materials with estimated memory use. Track what loads and unloads to investigate memory growth and potential memory leaks in your three.js scene.

![Resources panel in the Needle Inspector — textures, geometries and materials with memory estimates](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/9HBWd1PMn-bQoOHk4Mt0NQ.gif)

*   **Every texture, geometry and material** with memory estimates
*   **Load/unload tracking**: Spot resources that never get freed — memory leaks show up as rows that never disappear
*   **Draw calls, triangles, FPS and download size** at a glance

The free tier shows a preview of each group; the **full resource list** is part of [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Node Graphs & Rendering Insight](#node-graphs-rendering-insight)

See how your frame and shaders are actually built:

![Material node graph in the Needle Inspector — traversing and editing a three.js node material](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/DXpp8Bsku7cPBguuBD_2Hw.gif)

*   **Material Node Graphs**: Explore materials as node graphs (including three.js TSL / node materials)
*   **Render Graph**: Capture a frame and see every render call, pass, target and their dependencies

Viewing the full graph is free — **stepping into subgraphs and functions** and re-capturing frames is part of [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Code View — Shaders & Source](#code-view-shaders-source)

The code behind any selection, one click away:

![Code panel in the Needle Inspector — the source behind the selected object or material](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/XBuyTvCZ72dXacDzus2qUQ.gif)

*   **TSL, compiled shaders & three.js source**: Switch between the TSL code, the compiled vertex/fragment shaders and the three.js source of the selected material or object
*   **Follows your selection**: Lock the view to pin a source while you keep browsing — and copy out whatever you need

Your own three.js/object source and authored shaders are free. The inspector-**generated** sources — compiled shaders and reconstructed TSL — show a trimmed preview on the free tier; the full output is part of [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

![Node graph with the code panel side by side — TSL and three.js source for the selected material](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/Yv1pEJ9weTPRoRsq-Sfmiw.gif)

_Works side by side with the node graph — the source for exactly what you're looking at_

### [Built-in Assets Browser](#built-in-assets-browser)

Drop new content straight into a running scene — no downloads, no code changes:

![Assets browser in the Needle Inspector — browsing the asset library and dropping materials and HDRIs into a live three.js scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/OIAq3e4FBuBjQDZ8pnpZ1g.gif)

*   **HDRIs & Materials**: Browse a curated asset library with instant previews
*   **Drag & Drop**: Pull a material onto any mesh in the scene
*   **One-click Lighting**: Set an HDRI as the scene environment and background instantly

Browsing the library is free; **applying assets** is part of [Pro](#free-vs-pro).

### [Pop-Out Window](#pop-out-window)

Move the Inspector into a separate window to give your scene more space. Arrange the window beside your browser or on another monitor while you inspect the running scene. The pop-out window remembers its position and restores it when you reopen it.

![Needle Inspector panels in a separate pop-out window beside the running scene](https://cloud.needle.tools/-/media/mQUplopt_8cwxITmKOxLiw.gif)

### [Optimize a Mesh Without Leaving the Scene](#optimize-a-mesh-without-leaving-the-scene)

**New in 2.5:** send meshes straight to the **[Needle Mesh Baker](/docs/products/needle-mesh-baker)** without leaving the scene.

Drag objects from the hierarchy into a group — as many as you like — and bake each group on its own. A group comes back as one mesh, with transparent surfaces kept apart from opaque ones because they cannot share a material. A scene built from many small parts loses most of its draw calls along with its triangles.

The baked result lands in the running scene, and a toggle switches between the original and the baked version so you can compare the two in place. Adjust the triangle budget and bake again until it holds up.

Baking runs in your browser, and the mesh is not uploaded. Keeping a baked result needs the Mesh Baker; sending meshes over and looking at what comes back does not.

[Free vs Pro](#free-vs-pro)
---------------------------

The free version includes scene inspection, performance stats, and property editing on ordinary public websites. Pro adds editing on development servers, full resource lists and generated shader code, node-graph drill-down, AI tools, and export.

|  | Free | Pro |

| Scene hierarchy, search, live inspection | ![yes](/docs/inspector/check.svg) on supported sites | ![yes](/docs/inspector/check.svg) |

## Marble_World_Labs
World Labs tools for building 3D scenes from text and images: generate images,
estimate cameras and depth, generate new views, reconstruct Gaussian splats,
and extract meshes. Call list_projects first: it names the projects the user
may work in and which of these tools each can run. Every other tool takes a
project_id.

get an image into the project, use import_image for a file the client attached,
or create_image_upload and an HTTP PUT for a local file. A task's outputs are
assets too, so one task's output feeds the next by assetId.
The task tools use the project's World Labs Developer API credits: name the
project and say the tool will use credits before calling one. Each returns an
operation at once and can take from seconds to many minutes; poll get_operation
(it can wait up to 20 seconds per call) until done is true. Cameras use
OpenGL/Three.js conventions (right, up, back; quaternions in XYZW order), and a
frame's intrinsics describe its depth grid, which can differ from the source
image size. Use get_asset for a fresh download link when an earlier link has
expired. How the tasks fit together: https://docs.atlas.worldlabs.ai/how-to-use-atlas.md

## Thrixel
Thrixel turns text and images into editable, game-ready 3D assets (GLB).

Start with thrixel_start_project, named after what is being built. It is free,
and everything generated afterwards is filed under it automatically, so one
game's assets stay findable as a set instead of joining one flat list. Reopen
an earlier game with thrixel_list_projects then
thrixel_start_project(project_id=...).

Typical pipeline for a game prop:
  thrixel_create_model  -> a rough, editable, multi-part mesh
  thrixel_detail_model  -> high-resolution geometry + PBR texture
  thrixel_reduce_triangles  -> cut the triangle count to a game budget (free)

Use thrixel_sculpt_model instead of create_model for organic, single-piece
subjects (creatures, characters, plants) or when starting from a photo. Its
prompt becomes ONE three-quarter-view picture before it becomes 3D, so keep it
to one or two sentences about what that picture shows.

Reference images: thrixel_create_model takes up to 6 pictures (`images`:
file paths, URLs or data URIs) or the id of an image already in the account (reference_image_id), and
thrixel_sculpt_model takes one `image`. For a consistent SET of variants,
reuse the same reference_image_id or style_reference_submission_id on every
call.

Every job tool waits for completion by default, returns a download link for
the GLB plus a rendered thumbnail. Look at the thumbnail: if the
result is wrong, fix it with thrixel_edit_model or regenerate, rather than
carrying a bad asset forward. To resize, turn or move a finished model (any
kind, sculpts included) use thrixel_transform_model: it is free. Models arrive
with a longest side of 2 units (create) or about 1 (sculpt) unless created with
target_size_m (metres).

Glow: emissive materials survive only on create / edit results; sculpt,
detail and retexture output carry base colour, metallic, roughness and alpha.
Retexturing never changes geometry, so carved or relief detail stays.

Cost and limits worth knowing before a big batch:
  - detail / sculpt / texture / rig: a flat per-run price.
  - reduce_triangles / transform: free, and so is a smaller texture
    size picked on download (thrixel_download texture_size).
  - create / edit: METERED on actual model usage, charged after the
    run. Usually tens of cubes, and a complex one can cost more than a flat
    operation. These are not free.
  - Concurrent jobs are capped per plan, and EVERY running job counts,
    free ones (reduce_triangles, transform) included. Submitting past the cap
    returns an error naming your limit. Run batches in waves.
  - The cap only limits what you may have in flight. detail / sculpt /
    texture / rig run on one GPU lane shared across the service, so a big
    batch of them finishes over time whatever your cap;
    thrixel_account_status shows the lane depth.
  - A job still running when the wait ends is NOT an error: it keeps
    running and is charged when it completes. Check it with
    thrixel_job_status rather than submitting it again.
  - To reduce triangles on a model you already have, always use
    thrixel_reduce_triangles, never a second detail pass. It is free and faster.

For the actual numbers - this account's balance, cap and operation costs -
call thrixel_account_status.
They read from the service, so they are current; anything quoted from memory
eventually is not.

This connector runs on Thrixel's servers: it cannot read or write files on the user's computer. Images must be https URLs or data URIs, and thrixel_publish_game takes the game as data: its files, plus the Thrixel models it loads by submission_id.

  - Plan the asset list first and generate it, a few jobs at a time.
  - Build every object the player sees from a Thrixel model. Do not stand
    in boxes, spheres or other code-built shapes for a model that exists
    or is still generating; that is what makes a game look unfinished.
    Code-built geometry is for the ground, water, sky and effects.

**Sources read:** https://engine.needle.tools/docs/three/needle-devtools-for-threejs-chrome-extension/ and https://engine.needle.tools/docs/ai/needle-mcp-server/ (both HTTP 200, both pages fetched in full).

**a) Needle Inspector and install**
- It is a free Chrome extension that inspects three.js, React Three Fiber, and Needle Engine scenes with WebGL and WebGPU renderers. Pages describe it as "Chrome DevTools for three.js."
- Browsers: "Google Chrome or a Chromium-based browser." The page names Edge, Brave, Arc, and Opera. Firefox and Safari are not mentioned.
- Install: Chrome Web Store only. The docs give the store URL and "Add to Chrome." They mention no unpacked build, npm package, or other download.
- Usage: open a page with a three.js scene, click the Needle toolbar icon to enable the Inspector for that site (the page reloads), then pick objects in the hierarchy.
- Plain three.js/Vite: supported. The page lists "Any three.js-based framework," and says "Do I need Needle Engine? No. The inspector works on any three.js scene." Localhost and LAN dev servers "including projects served with Vite or webpack" are supported.
- Minimum version and setup: the page only says "modern three.js versions." It does not mention `__THREE_DEVTOOLS__` or any app-side hook. Detection "can vary with the three.js version and how the site creates its scene."

**b) Free vs Pro**
- Free: scene hierarchy, search, live inspection, performance stats, free-fly camera, node graphs (viewing), code view (your own source), and property editing on ordinary public websites. Also asset library browsing, a limited camera timeline, and resource previews.
- Pro: live property editing on development servers (localhost, LAN, and supported dev/preview/staging hosts), "Inspector MCP tools & AI editing," "Save Edits (JSON/text)," GLB export, full resource list, node-graph drill-down, full generated shader code, longer camera animations with JSON import/export, and applying assets.
- Saving edits back to source: the page's workflow is File → Save Edits (JSON), then the user or an AI agent applies the JSON to source. Saving edits requires Pro. The page also says that with MCP, an agent can call `get_edits` to pull pending edits and apply them to source.
- Price: the page does not state a price. It says the price "is always shown in the extension (Get Pro in the toolbar)," and that it is "a one-time purchase — no subscription." It is also included with Needle Engine Pro licenses.
- Where to buy: https://cloud.needle.tools/buy/needle-inspector-pro, or the Get Pro button in the toolbar. Purchase requires signing in or creating a Needle account.

**c) Needle MCP server with Claude Code**
- Exact command: `claude mcp add --scope user --transport stdio needle -- npx -y needle-cloud mcp`
- Transport: stdio (the default). The page also documents an HTTP alternative: run `npx needle-cloud start` and connect to `http://localhost:8424/mcp`. The page says the stdio setup "also supports Needle Inspector tools."
- Then start or restart Claude Code and check the connection with `/mcp`.
- The stdio command "reuses or starts the shared local server at localhost:8424." Node/npx must be available.
- Browser requirement: Inspector-specific tools need the Inspector open in Chrome. The page says "When you have the Needle Inspector open in Chrome, additional tools become available." Built-in MCP tools work without it. The page does not say the browser must be visible or that DevTools must be open.
- Account or licence: the MCP setup steps mention no login or key. The Inspector MCP tools and AI editing require Pro, and buying Pro requires a Needle account.
- Headless Chromium or remote Linux: the pages do not address this at all.

**d) MCP tools**
- Built-in, always available (no Inspector needed): Search (Needle Engine docs and forum, semantic), Load Needle Skill, Get Project Path, Get Scene Path, Get Web Project Path, Get Log Path, Read File, Search Files, List Files, Read Log, Read glTF/GLB.
- Inspector tools: the page says the agent "reads the hierarchy, inspects objects, changes properties, and pulls your pending edits (`get_edits`)." It also says changes "appear instantly in your browser." The full list is in the Inspector settings, and the page does not enumerate it. Screenshots, camera control, and materials/cameras as dedicated tools are not named.
- Blender-specific tools exist but do not apply to three.js.

**e) Limitations relevant to your setup**
- No Chrome Web Store access: the only documented install path is the Web Store, so there is no documented way to install the extension otherwise.
- Headless or no desktop: not mentioned. The docs assume a browser with the extension running. Whether a headless Chromium can load the extension is not stated.
- Dev-server editing: Pro only. Edits can be lost: "a reload or hot update can replace edited objects."
- Detection depends on the three.js version and how the site creates its scene.
- Data: inspection runs in the browser. With your own MCP client, scene context goes directly to that client, not through Needle Cloud.
- Pro is a one-time purchase, but the price is not on the page.
